findings.scenario: A developer edits analyzer/PDG code under gitnexus/src and runs `node --import tsx bench/impact-pdg/measure.mjs` locally (the documented build-free usage) while an older gitnexus/dist/ is on disk. cliChildArgs sees that dist/cli/index.js exists and runs the analyze child from the stale compiled CLI. The in-process LocalBackend, imported from src, then reads an index produced by old code. The precision/recall/mutation numbers reflect the old analyzer, and nothing warns about it.
findings.evidence: `function cliChildArgs(rest) { return fs.existsSync(DIST_CLI) ? [DIST_CLI, ...rest] : [TSX_CLI, CLI_ENTRY, ...rest]; }` picks dist only because the file exists. There is no freshness check against src and no opt-out. Before this change the analyze entry always ran from src/cli/index.ts via tsx.
findings.recommendation: Only prefer dist when it is requested explicitly (for example an env flag set by the mutation workflow) or when dist is newer than src. Otherwise print a clear notice saying which CLI entry was used, so a stale build cannot silently skew local bench results.
